metadata.title: PCR-999: Addgene Standard PCR Protocol
metadata.purpose: Amplify a specific DNA region in vitro using Taq DNA polymerase through repeated heating and cooling cycles. Based on the Addgene standard PCR protocol for a 50 uL Taq-style reaction.
metadata.scope: Standard endpoint PCR using Taq polymerase. Not validated for qPCR, RT-PCR, or high-fidelity cloning workflows.
beforeYouBegin: Keep all reagents on ice during setup to maintain enzyme activity.
Use thin-walled PCR tubes for optimal heat transfer in the thermal cycler.
Design primers using tools such as Primer3. Ensure primers are 18-24 nt, 40-60% GC content, with Tm within 5 degrees C of each other.
For multiple reactions, prepare a master mix containing all shared components (except primers and template) with 10% extra volume to account for pipetting loss.
Use a clean workspace with dedicated pre-PCR pipettes and aerosol-resistant tips.

materials.name: Template DNA
materials.specification: 10-500 ng total; plasmid DNA, genomic DNA, cDNA, or purified amplicon

materials.name: 10X Taq buffer with MgCl2
materials.specification: Provides optimal chemical environment; divalent cations stabilize interactions
materials.storage: Store at -20 degrees C; keep on ice during use

materials.name: dNTP mix (10 mM each nucleotide)
materials.specification: Equal molar ratio of dATP, dTTP, dGTP, dCTP; final 200 uM each in reaction
materials.storage: Store at -20 degrees C; avoid repeated freeze-thaw

materials.name: Forward primer
materials.specification: Final 0.5 uM in reaction; anneals upstream (5') of target segment
materials.storage: Store at -20 degrees C; keep on ice during use

materials.name: Reverse primer
materials.specification: Final 0.5 uM in reaction; anneals downstream (3') of target segment
materials.storage: Store at -20 degrees C; keep on ice during use

materials.name: Taq DNA polymerase
materials.specification: Heat-resistant enzyme from Thermus aquaticus; 1 U per 50 uL reaction; optimal activity around 70 degrees C
materials.storage: Store at -20 degrees C; keep on ice; do NOT vortex

materials.name: 25 mM MgCl2 (optional)
materials.specification: For optimization if PCR fails; add to increase Mg2+ concentration

materials.name: DMSO (optional)
materials.specification: For GC-rich templates; aids denaturation of secondary structures

equipment.name: Thin-walled PCR tubes
equipment.settings: 0.2 mL thin-walled tubes for optimal heat transfer

tables.title: 50 uL Reaction Setup
tables.note: Volumes are for a single 50 uL reaction. For master mix preparation, multiply each volume by (N + 10%) where N is the number of reactions.

tables.title: Cycling Program
tables.note: Annealing temperature should be set approximately 5 degrees C below the primer melting temperature (Tm). Extension time depends on amplicon size at approximately 1-2 kb per minute for Taq polymerase.

tables.title: Master Mix Calculation Example (7 reactions)
tables.note: Multiply reagent volumes by (number of reactions + 10% overage). Primers are added individually to each tube and are NOT included in the master mix.

tables.title: Primer Dilution Guide
rows: Add dH2O in uL equal to (nanomoles x 10) to the lyophilized primer pellet
Dilute 1:10 from 100 uM stock (100 uL stock + 900 uL dH2O)

steps.action: Design primers using a tool such as Primer3. Primers should be complementary to sequences flanking the target region, annealing upstream (5') and downstream (3') of the DNA segment to be amplified.
steps.expectedResult: Primers designed with appropriate length, GC content, and Tm.

steps.action: Place thin-walled PCR tubes on ice.
steps.expectedResult: PCR tubes chilled and ready for reagent addition.

steps.action: Set up 50 uL reaction on ice: add 2 uL template DNA (10-500 ng), 5 uL 10X Taq buffer with MgCl2, 1 uL dNTP mix (10 mM each), 2.5 uL forward primer (10 uM), 2.5 uL reverse primer (10 uM), 0.2 uL Taq DNA polymerase (5 U/uL), and 36.8 uL sterile dH2O.
steps.criticalNotes: Keep all reagents on ice during setup.
steps.expectedResult: 50 uL reaction assembled in PCR tube.

steps.action: Place reaction tubes in the PCR machine.
steps.expectedResult: Tubes seated in thermal cycler block.

steps.action: Set the annealing temperature to approximately 5 degrees C below the primer melting temperature (Tm).

parameters.rawText: Annealing: Tm minus 5 degrees C (typically ~55 degrees C)

steps.action: Set the extension step to 1-2 minutes per kilobase of expected product length, depending on polymerase proofreading capability.
steps.expectedResult: Extension time configured based on amplicon size.

steps.action: Initial denaturation: heat to 94 degrees C for 2 minutes to fully denature the template DNA and break hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs.
steps.expectedResult: Template DNA fully denatured into single strands.

steps.action: Denature at 94 degrees C for 30 seconds.
steps.expectedResult: Double-stranded DNA separated into single strands.

steps.action: Anneal primers at 55 degrees C (or 5 degrees C below Tm) for 30 seconds. Forward and reverse primers bind to their complementary sequences on the single-stranded template; DNA polymerase binds to the primer-template duplex.
steps.expectedResult: Primers annealed to complementary template sequences.

steps.action: Extend DNA at 72 degrees C for 1 minute per kilobase. Taq polymerase synthesizes new DNA strands by adding dNTPs complementary to the template, starting from the 3' end of each primer.
steps.expectedResult: New DNA strands synthesized from primers.

steps.action: Repeat steps 8-10 (denature, anneal, extend) for 25-30 cycles.

repeat.notes: 25-30 cycles; adjust based on template abundance

steps.expectedResult: Target DNA amplified exponentially over 25-30 cycles.

steps.action: Final extension at 72 degrees C for 5 minutes to ensure complete synthesis of all partially extended products.
steps.expectedResult: All newly synthesized strands fully extended.

steps.action: Run 2 uL of PCR product on an agarose gel to check size and concentration of the PCR product.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Single band at expected amplicon size
No target-size band in no-template control

steps.expectedResult: Single band at expected size confirmed on gel.

steps.action: Multiply each reagent volume by the number of PCR reactions needed, plus 10% extra to account for pipetting error.
steps.expectedResult: Master mix volumes calculated for N + 10% reactions.

steps.action: Combine calculated volumes in a single tube: 10X Taq buffer, dNTP mix, template DNA, sterile dH2O, and Taq DNA polymerase. For example, for 7 reactions: 38.5 uL buffer, 7.7 uL dNTPs, 15.4 uL template, 283.3 uL water, 1.54 uL Taq polymerase.
steps.criticalNotes: Add polymerase last. Do NOT vortex.
steps.expectedResult: All shared reagents combined in master mix tube.

steps.action: Mix the master mix contents gently by pipetting up and down. Keep the tube on ice.
steps.criticalNotes: Do NOT vortex — mix by gentle pipetting only.

steps.action: Add 2.5 uL forward primer and 2.5 uL reverse primer to each thin-walled PCR tube individually. Do NOT add primers to the master mix.
steps.criticalNotes: Primers are added individually to each tube, NOT included in the master mix.
steps.expectedResult: Forward and reverse primers dispensed into each reaction tube.

steps.action: Add 45 uL of master mix to each PCR tube (50 uL total reaction volume minus 2.5 uL forward primer minus 2.5 uL reverse primer).
steps.expectedResult: Each tube contains 50 uL total reaction volume.

steps.action: Secure tube tops and tap gently to mix contents. Place tubes in the PCR machine and run the cycling program.
steps.expectedResult: All reaction tubes sealed, mixed, and loaded into thermal cycler.

controls.name: No-template control (NTC)
controls.description: Replace template DNA with sterile dH2O to detect reagent or environmental contamination. No target-size band expected.

controls.name: Positive control
controls.description: Use a known template that reliably amplifies to verify master mix, cycling program, and detection are working. Expected band should appear.

expectedOutputs: Single band at the expected amplicon size on agarose gel.
Positive control band at expected size.
Complete run record with sample map, reagent details, cycling program, and gel image.

troubleshooting.cause: Wrong annealing temperature, missing component, degraded template, inhibitors in template preparation
troubleshooting.solution: Verify setup; lower annealing temperature step-wise; add 1 uL 25 mM MgCl2 and/or 1 uL DMSO per reaction; use fresh enzyme; dilute template to reduce inhibitors

troubleshooting.cause: Annealing temperature too low, excess template or primer, nonspecific primer binding
troubleshooting.solution: Increase annealing temperature step-wise by 1-2 degrees C; reduce template or primer concentration; consider hot-start polymerase; redesign primers
Reduce cycle number; improve template quality; optimize annealing temperature; load less product on gel
Reduce primer concentration to 0.2-0.3 uM; redesign primers to minimize 3' complementarity

troubleshooting.cause: Strong secondary structures in GC-rich regions resist denaturation
troubleshooting.solution: Increase denaturation time; add 1 uL DMSO per reaction; consider specialized GC-rich PCR kits

safety: Ethidium bromide or alternative DNA stains may be mutagenic — wear gloves when handling gels and follow institutional disposal rules.
UV transilluminators emit UV radiation — use eye and skin protection.
